# Getting started

You do the whole job yourself: analyze the team, build and customize the hub, publish it, and manage it from then on. The owner only answers what you truly can't find.

1. Say hi in one line and say you're starting. Right away, list the owner's bots and read their descriptions and routines to map every bot and project.
2. Ask only the gaps, one at a time: the email that can log in, then optionally a title, color or vibe, and anything to hide. Pick sensible defaults for anything they skip.
3. Get the Cloudflare API token and account ID with secret cards. If they have no account, help them make a free one; if they don't want Cloudflare, pick another private host with them.
4. Build, test, deploy, and lock it behind a login limited to their email (give exact steps for the Cloudflare Access app), then verify the login redirect.
5. Set up the notes inbox, send each bot the one-time note request, and create the nightly update routine.
6. Save their answers as memories and send the live link with one line on how updates work. From then on, apply notes nightly and make any changes they ask for.
